bucket_reason: Priority call: observe is done at LOW confidence. The exact rules cover 99.3% of record moves, but the macro level and the non-halting argument are open, so proof work waits.
question: W4-4 and its three sibling starts (188, 450, 564) share one defect-list mechanism: fund one ~2 h rules stage to close the abstract model and probe the macro hierarchy, or park the family with R4/#32?

options.label: Fund one ~2 h rules stage for the whole family
options.consequence: Rule the 5 unruled event families (the 6-step end rule, the first eat bounce, LA>RA run-offs, RA>LA full returns, merges; 668 of 98,334 moves to 1e10). Then build an abstract list-machine simulator, check it against the TM for all four starts to 1e10, and use it to look for the hierarchy and an invariant candidate. Output: an exact model plus a go/no-go on proof.md, but no invariant guaranteed.

options.label: Park 156/188/450/564 now
options.consequence: No compute. All four go to STUCK with these notes (window lemmas, E, the L transducer, coverage files). Work resumes from scripts/ if a multi-level-counter method appears (e.g. from R4/#32).

options.label: Go straight for the invariant
options.consequence: Open-ended (several stages). An invariant written now would rest on 668 unruled moves and on a parity law that already fails at 17 of 60 eat starts.

rationale: Rules L and E already cover 99.3% of moves; the rest looks like a few fixed shapes.
One model serves 4 holdouts (near-twin orbits of one table).
The list stays short (2-13 separators to 1e10); park if the stage finds no invariant handle.
